title: Customer-facing RCA and status page update playbook for inter-region capacity regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a cross-region traffic surge on 2026-03-10 we observed elevated 503/timeout rates for hosted inference endpoints in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Root cause traces to a deployed kernel memory growth regression combined with autoscaler density rules that prevented timely node allocation. This ticket is the canonical playbook for customer-facing communications, status page updates, and the actionable RCA items required to close the postmortem. Deliverables: (1) final statuspage incident update and archived timeline, (2) enterprise customer email and account-team brief, (3) verified action items assigned with owners and dates, (4) runbook/update to prevent recurrence.
investigation_summary: What we learned: a kernel optimization change (PR #1462) reduced per-token CPU but increased peak GPU-side pinned memory under bursty short-sequence workloads. Autoscaler density rules (policy v2) treat GPU pool utilization as a hard cap and require a cooldown window before scaling additional nodes. During the surge, memory growth caused multiple serving nodes to evict shards and return 503s; autoscaler did not add new nodes quickly enough because the cooldown and bin-packing thresholds deferred action. Mitigations applied during the incident: rolled back PR #1462, increased autoscaler reactive threshold, and temporarily disabled bin-packing for affected pools. Next steps: permanent autoscaler rule changes, kernel memory fixes with benchmarks, and additional telemetry on per-container GPU memory footprints.

customer_comms_drafts: Statuspage initial (public): We are investigating elevated error rates affecting text-generation endpoints in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Our engineering team is actively triaging and applying mitigations. Updates will follow every 30-60 minutes. Incident ID: RWI-2026-0310-01. Link to incident timeline: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RWI-2026-0310-01

Statuspage resolved + short RCA (public): The incident affecting text-generation endpoints has been resolved. Root cause: a recent runtime kernel change increased peak GPU memory usage under bursty short-sequence loads; autoscaler density rules delayed additional node allocation. Mitigations: roll back of kernel change and autoscaler threshold adjustments. Full RCA and action items will be published on our postmortem page within 3 business days.

Enterprise email (customers with SLA/enterprise teams): Subject: Incident RWI-2026-0310-01 — Summary, Impact, and Next Steps. Body: Hi <CustomerName>, on 2026-03-10 some requests to hosted inference endpoints experienced higher error rates and increased latency. We identified the cause as a runtime memory regression combined with autoscaler behavior under surge. We rolled back the change and adjusted autoscaler rules; your workloads are not expected to be impacted further. Attachments: timeline, impact summary (tokens/hour), mitigations applied, and planned fixes with ETA. Account team contact: <AM Name>.

Account team brief (internal): One-pager for AMs with customer-specific impact table (start/end, affected endpoints, observed 503 rate, possible billing adjustments if applicable) and recommended talking points: apology, steps taken, expected mitigating controls, and offer of technical remediation call if requested.
